acceptance_criteria: Public, documented types: `pub enum HoleDepth { Blind(f64), ThroughAll }` and `pub enum HoleKind { Simple { diameter: f64 }, Counterbore { diameter: f64, cb_diameter: f64, cb_depth: f64 } }`. Blind depth is measured from `at.origin` along the drill direction to the flat hole bottom (no drill point). Counterbore depth is measured the same way.

`Kernel::hole(&self, s: &Self::Shape, at: Axis, kind: HoleKind, depth: HoleDepth) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented: `at.origin` is the hole's center on the start face and `at.dir` (normalized first) points into the material. `ThroughAll` cuts through the whole solid along the direction from `at.origin`. Implemented for `OcctKernel`; any new shim function is `noexcept`, catches C++ exceptions, and rejects a result `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds invalid.

Tests (behind `occt`), box `make_box((0, 0, 0), (40, 30, 20))` (volume 24000), volumes within a relative 1e-6, boxes within 1e-6: simple Ø6, blind 10, at (20, 15, 20) along −Z: volume 24000 − 90π ≈ 23717.2567; 8 faces; bounding box unchanged. simple Ø6, through all, same axis: volume 24000 − 180π ≈ 23434.5133; 7 faces. counterbore Ø6 / Ø11 depth 6, through all, same axis: volume 24000 − (181.5π + 126π) ≈ 23033.9603; 9 faces. counterbore Ø6 / Ø11 depth 6, blind 10, same axis: volume 24000 − (181.5π + 36π) ≈ 23316.7036; 10 faces. simple Ø6, blind 10, on a side face: at (0, 15, 10) along +X: volume ≈ 23717.2567; the hole bottom face's box is (10, 12, 7)–(10, 18, 13). the input solid is unchanged (volume 24000, 6 faces).

Errors, each with a test and never a panic: a diameter, blind depth, `cb_diameter` or `cb_depth` that is zero, negative or not finite; `cb_diameter` ≤ `diameter`; a blind depth ≤ `cb_depth`; a zero-length or non-finite `at.dir`; a non-finite `at.origin`. These are `InvalidInput`, checked before the backend. A hole whose axis misses the solid (at (100, 15, 20) along −Z) is an error (`InvalidInput`, `Backend` or `EmptyResult`), not a silent no-op.
No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies. Every new `unsafe` block is in `ffi` and documented; the doc comment cites the OCCT reference documentation of the calls used.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
